one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled or known events fall in the window. (1) Q3-2026 results, expected about 2026-11-02 before the open per Earnings Whispers [28]. The date is not yet confirmed by the company, but Generac's Q3 reports have historically come in late October or early November, so the report very likely falls before 11-08. Q3 consensus is EPS $2.43 and revenue $1.327B, and estimates were cut into the print (14 down vs 3 up revisions in 30 days [4]). Residential faced a quiet outage environment (Q2 outages >30% below baseline [2]), so a soft residential quarter is largely expected. The call should be the first full discussion of the Amazon agreement ($2.4B of 2027-28 deliveries [3]) and Sussex/Belvidere ramp timing, and is likely to firm 2027 data-center visibility. That is a modest positive skew, but GNRC's earnings-week moves are large in both directions (weekly bars [21]: +17.4% in the Q1 week ending 2026-05-01; -2.4% in the Q2 week ending 2026-07-31, with an intraweek low of $187.55, 7% below the prior close). (2) Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, FL on the night of Oct 9 with 105 mph winds (WPTV [26]; Polymarket Florida-landfall market at 99.7% [25]), after Friday's close. Outages in the Panhandle support near-term home-standby sentiment and Q4/Q1 orders, but a moderate Cat 1-2 Panhandle hit is not a 2017/2021-type outage season, and some of this was likely priced on Oct 8-9. Momentum is positive (from $187 on Sep 11 to $225 [21]). I set the median at $227, only slightly above spot, with a fat-tailed spread: a 50/50 mix of 13% and 21% one-month lognormal sigmas around the stock's usual ~16% monthly vol (56%/3.5), widened for the earnings print.

fair_value.method: Blend of 70% forward P/E ($14.38 NTM EPS at Oct-2027 x 19x segment-mix peer multiple = $273) and 30% DCF (WACC 11.4%, terminal growth 3%, = $144); the DCF is punished by a 5.24% risk-free rate, the P/E reflects how the market prices data-center growth.

inputs_detail.derivation: Alpha Vantage 19-analyst mean (up from $11.82 30 days earlier after the Amazon deal); StockAnalysis/S&P Global shows $12.97, so $12.67 is the lower of the two

$12.67 x 1.18. Data-center revenue ~$1.9B 2027 (JPM visibility) rising past $3B in 2028 (Wells Fargo), both as reported by Stocktwits [23], consistent with Amazon initial deliveries of $2.4B over 2027-28 [3] and the capacity-tripling path [2]: ~+$1.1B revenue x ~16% EBIT margin (adj. EBITDA margin guide 18.5-19.5% ex-tariff [2] less ~3.5% D&A) x (1-23.25% tax [6]) / ~60M shares = ~+$2.3/share = +18%, residential assumed flat. Below the Street-implied ~+28% for 2028 (StockAnalysis 3y EPS growth fcst 36.8%/yr [6] compounded against +52.8% 2026 [5] and +31% 2027 [4]) and above TIKR's 15.5% normalized EPS CAGR [30]
On 2027-10-09 the next twelve months are Q4-2027 plus Q1-Q3 2028, i.e. about one quarter of FY2027 and three quarters of FY2028: 0.25 x 12.67 + 0.75 x 14.95 = $14.38

Segment-mix weighted peer multiple: about 45% of 2027 sales residential (Q2-26 residential $621M of $1,174M = 53% [1], diluting as data center grows), priced like the residential-durable peers AOS 14.47x / LII 14.43x (mean 14.5x); ~25% other C&I priced like CMI 15.94x; ~30% data center priced like VRT 30.75 / ETN 28.47 / NVT 28.67 / POWL 29.74 / CAT 27.78 (mean 29.1x). 0.45x14.5 + 0.25x15.9 + 0.30x29.1 = 19.2x, rounded to 19.0x. It sits inside the 14.4-79.1x peer range and below the 28.6x median, and below GNRC's current 21.7x [6] because the forward base by then is more of the peak data-center ramp

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: WACC 11.4% (rf 5.24%, ERP 4.20%, Blume beta 1.62, kd 5.2% after tax, D/V 9.6%); revenue 2027 $6.40B, 2028 $7.40B, +6%/yr 2029-31; adj EBITDA margin 19.5% fading to 18.5%; capex 4.5% of sales; D&A 3.5%; NWC 15% of incremental sales; tax 23.25%; terminal growth 3%; net debt $0.55B; 59.9M diluted shares; valued at Oct-2027

inputs_detail.derivation: Blume adjustment of 5y raw beta 1.92: 0.67 x 1.92 + 0.33 = 1.62; cost of equity 5.24% + 1.62 x 4.20% = 12.03%

inputs_detail.input: After-tax cost of debt and weights
inputs_detail.derivation: Pre-tax 6.74% = 10y 5.24% + 150bp spread (judgment), x (1-23.25% effective tax [6]); weights from market cap $13.29B and total debt $1.41B [6]. WACC = 0.904 x 12.03% + 0.096 x 5.17% = 11.37%
2027 $6.40B + ~$1.0B data-center growth (JPM ~$1.9B 2027 to Wells Fargo >$3B 2028, as reported by [23]; Amazon $2.4B 2027-28 deliveries [3]); residential flat

Amazon framework runs up to $8B through 2033 [3], but OEM capacity additions (lead times expected to be the binding constraint only through at least 2027 [27]) limit data-center pricing and share gains; residential grows low-to-mid single digits, as in the investor-day mid-teens framework fading [30]

FY26 guide 18.5-19.5% excluding tariff refunds [2]; investor day 2028 framework EBITDA $1.25-1.45B on $6.2-6.6B sales [30]; fade reflects genset price inflation ($450-600/kW vs $380-420/kW in 2023 [27]) normalising as capacity comes on
Management: capex ~4.5% of 2026 net sales, 'comfortably below' 5%
TTM D&A $214.8M / revenue $4.44B = 4.8% including acquisition amortization; tangible D&A assumed ~3.5% as revenue scales faster than the asset base
TTM operating cash flow $548M vs FCF $379M [6] shows inventory-heavy model; 15% of revenue growth absorbed in NWC
From the inputs above; ties to the 2026 FCF guide of ~$350M [2] and the investor-day >$1.5B three-year FCF framework [30] (0.35+0.50+0.68 = $1.53B)
Q2-26 diluted 59.64M [1] + ~0.3M treasury-method dilution from Amazon warrant (1.69M shares at $200.93 [3])
Nominal long-run GDP-like growth, below the 5.24% risk-free rate

bear.story: Residential stays depressed (quiet outage seasons, housing/consumer weakness; Polymarket prices a 32.5% chance of US recession by end-2027 on a thin $10k market [24]). Data-center ramp slips on capacity or quality issues at Sussex/Belvidere, or hyperscalers shift mix to Caterpillar/Cummins/Rolls-Royce as OEM capacity catches up [27]. 2027 EPS lands near the $11.3 low estimate [4] and the market pays ~13-14x NTM about $11-11.5 = ~$150, back below the pre-Amazon $175-187 range [21].

base.story: 2027 EPS around the $12.7-13.0 consensus [4][5] as data-center revenue reaches roughly $1.9B [23] and residential is flat to slightly up. The market looks through to 2028 but trims the multiple toward a segment-mix ~16-17x NTM as data-center growth peaks and the DCF value under 5%+ rates acts as gravity. That gives ~$235, in line with blended fair value.

bull.story: Capacity triples on time [2], data-center revenue tracks past $3B for 2028 (Wells Fargo per [23]), and the first hyperscaler's 2027-28 terms plus further hyperscaler awards extend backlog into 2029. An active 2027 hurricane season revives home standby. 2028 EPS of $16-17 at 20-21x NTM gives ~$340, between the $288 mean and the $375 top Street target [5].

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 14.4x (LII) to 79.1x (BE), 10 of 12 between 14.4x and 30.8x; EV/EBITDA (TTM basis, forward not available from free sources) 10.4x (AOS) to 197.7x (BE), median 26.0x
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 19.0x NTM (Oct-2027) P/E, about 33% below the 28.6x peer median and inside the range. GNRC trades at 21.7x forward P/E and 22.7x TTM EV/EBITDA today [6], also below the medians.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount is a mix effect, not a call that GNRC will underperform. The peer set holds two groups that trade very differently: residential-durable and engine names (AOS 14.5x, LII 14.4x, CMI 15.9x) and data-center electrical names (VRT, ETN, NVT, POWL, CAT 27.8-30.8x). In 2027 roughly 70% of GNRC sales are still residential or traditional C&I, and only about 30% data center. Weighting the two groups' mean multiples by that mix gives 19.2x. Three things should keep the discount through the horizon. (a) Residential earnings depend on outages and are volatile (Q2-26 outages >30% below baseline cut residential growth guidance [2]). (b) Customer concentration rises: the Amazon framework of up to $8B comes with a warrant [3]. (c) Equity risk is higher: 5y beta is 1.92 [6]. GEV and BE are AI-power momentum outliers and are not used to set the multiple.

thesis_break_reason: $160 is about 29% below spot and clearly below the $173-187 range where the stock traded before the Amazon agreement (Aug to mid-Sep 2026 [21]). A sustained close there would mean the market has written off the 2027-28 data-center ramp (delivery slippage, a cancelled or renegotiated hyperscaler tranche, margin problems at the new plants) or residential has entered a demand slump like the 2022-23 destock. Neither is ordinary volatility for a 56%-vol stock that is already back near fair value.

How much of Amazon's up-to-$8B framework converts and on what timeline beyond the $2.4B 2027-28 initial deliveries; concentration risk
Data-center genset pricing once Caterpillar, Cummins and Rolls-Royce capacity additions arrive (lead times expected to bind only through at least 2027)
Residential home-standby demand in a low-outage environment, plus consumer and housing sensitivity at 5%+ long rates
Whether the market keeps paying for data-center growth as the cycle matures, versus a DCF value near $145 at an 11.4% WACC
Q3-2026 date and print are not yet confirmed; estimates were cut into the quarter
reasoning: Facts: Q2-26 sales +11% to $1.17B, C&I +29%, adjusted EPS $2.91 including ~$71M tariff refunds [1]. FY26 guide is mid-to-high-teens growth and 18.5-19.5% adj. EBITDA margin ex-refunds, ~$450M data-center revenue, ~$350M FCF, and a $1.6B data-center backlog of which $1.35B delivers in 2027 [1][2]. On 2026-09-16 Generac signed an Amazon supply agreement of up to $8B, with $2.4B of initial deliveries in 2027-28 and a 1.69M-share warrant at $200.93 [3]. The stock spiked from ~$175 toward $250 intraday, then settled at $207 that week [21][31]. The 2027 EPS consensus rose from $11.82 to $12.67 in 30 days [4]. Lane work: Substack/Stocktwits flow shows an 18% volume spike and 'extremely bullish' retail sentiment around the deal [22][23]. That is a contrarian caution, since sentiment was already euphoric while the stock gave back part of the spike. Trade research says large-genset lead times are 18-24 months and prices are $450-600/kW (vs $380-420 in 2023), binding through at least 2027 [27]. That supports 2027 pricing but flags normalisation risk afterwards. Job postings show new Sussex engineering roles posted the day after the deal [29], consistent with the capacity build. Insider Form 4s show only small 10b5-1 sales [32], so no signal. Prediction markets put the Florida 2026 landfall at 99.7% (Isaias) [25] and US recession by end-2027 at 32.5% on thin volume [24]. Valuation: a 19x segment-mix forward P/E on NTM EPS at Oct-2027 gives $273. A DCF at an 11.4% WACC (5.24% risk-free [19], 4.20% ERP [20]) gives only $144. Blended 70/30, fair value is ~$235, about 4% above spot, against a $288 Street mean target [5]. The ladder is a three-scenario lognormal mixture (bear $150 / 25%, base $235 / 50%, bull $340 / 25%, component sigmas 0.32 / 0.24 / 0.27). It has a median near $235 and an overall log-sd of ~0.40, below the 56% realized vol, which is inflated by the September deal jump, but with fat tails kept (P>=$450 4%, P<$135 10%). Limits: Twelve Data fundamentals/estimates endpoints and Alpha Vantage COMPANY_OVERVIEW are paywalled, so I used free endpoints only. Reddit refused fetching, Google Trends returned 429, poweroutage.us and ZipRecruiter returned 403, and Manifold had no GNRC markets. I did not attempt X (login wall). sec.gov refused a generic User-Agent, so I read filings with WebFetch. Because the mandated 12-peer comps set and the filings need data citations, only 8 of 32 sources (25%) are in-lane, short of the 60% target. The in-lane sources unlikely to be found by other lanes are [22][23][24][25][27][28][29][30].
